newsitem.title: USA: NFL AMERICAN FOOTBALL-SEIFERT RESIGNS AS 49ER COACH. [CORRECTED 2:57 GMT]
newsitem.headline: NFL AMERICAN FOOTBALL-SEIFERT RESIGNS AS 49ER COACH. [CORRECTED 2:57 GMT]

text.p: George Seifert, who won two Super Bowls but could never emerge from the shadows of predecessor Bill Walsh, resigned Wednesday as coach of the San Francisco 49ers.
Seifert, 57, reportedly will be replaced by 40-year-old Steve Mariucci, whose only head coaching experience was this past season as head man at the University of California.
"I consider myself one of the lucky people in the world in my profession," Seifert said in announcing his resignation.

"It has been an important and fun time in my life. I feel pride in the things I've accomplished," said Seifert (corrects), adding that he could have stayed with the 49ers, but "there's a sense and a feeling that there needs to be some changes made."

Seifert spent eight seasons under Walsh as an assistant and another eight as head coach. Despite two championships and the best winning percentage in NFL history (108-35), Seifert was never anointed with the "genius" status afforded Walsh.

This season, Walsh served as an administrative assistant to the coaching staff. But players often referred to him as "coach Walsh" and he had considerable input in game preparation and play-calling, which created an uneasy situation with offensive coordinator Marc Trestman.
The 49ers went 12-4 this season, but lost twice to the Carolina Panthers, a second-year expansion team that unseated them for the NFC West title.
San Francisco defeated Philadelphia in a wild-card playoff game but lost the following week to the Green Bay Packers.

Seifert is one of just eight coaches to win two Super Bowls. In 1989, he succeeded Walsh and guided the 49ers to their second straight Super Bowl crown, joining Baltimore's Don McCafferty as the only first-year coach to win a Super Bowl.
He set records by reaching 50, 75, and 100 victories faster than any coach.
Mariucci's California team was 6-6 and lost in the Aloha Bowl to Navy. Mariucci is considered an offensive-minded coach, but his team ranked 105th nationally in total defence last season.
Mariucci spent four seasons as an assistant coach with the Packers, working strictly with quarterbacks. He is credited with helping Brett Favre become one of the premier quarterbacks in the NFL.
